content: 1. Maraviroc levels can be influenced by the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Therapeutic drug concentrations should be monitored as indicated, or the dosage of the P-gp substrate should be reduced and titrated to achieve the desired clinical effect. 2. Serious interactions may occur between elivaldogene autotemcel and maraviroc. Either drug may decrease the effects of the other. Alternative drugs should be considered. Patients should avoid taking antiretroviral medications for at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization therapy, during the therapy, and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 3. Maraviroc is contraindicated with the combination of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF. This combination is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be co-administered with other antiretrovirals. 4. Maraviroc and enalapril may increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution should be used, and patients should be monitored closely due to an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 5. Maraviroc may increase the levels or effects of encainide by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 6. Encorafenib may affect maraviroc levels by inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 7. Enzalutamide may decrease maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered to avoid this interaction. 8. Maraviroc and eprosartan may increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored closely due to an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 9. Erythromycin base increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered to avoid this interaction. 10. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate formulations also increase maraviroc levels through similar mechanisms. Alternative drugs are recommended. 11. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 12. Maraviroc and esmolol may increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Patients should be monitored closely due to an increased risk of orthostatic hypotension. 13. Conjugated synthetic estrogens, esterified estrogens, and estropipate increase maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. 14. Ethacrynic acid and maraviroc may increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Close monitoring is recommended. 15. Etonogestrel increases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. 16. Etravirine decreases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 17. Etynodiol increases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. 18. Fedratinib increases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary, and close monitoring is recommended. 19. Felodipine increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 20. Maraviroc and fenoldopam may increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism.
